questions.q: What does `terraform apply` create for the very first time in this lesson?
options: Only the AWS S3 bucket
The resource group, VNet/subnet, ACR, AKS cluster, and the storefront Helm release, all in one apply
Just a single Azure VM
Nothing; it only validates the configuration
questions.explain: All six resources from Lesson 4's configuration are created together, including the Helm release onto the brand-new cluster.

questions.q: What happens after `git push origin main` in this lesson?
options: Theo manually runs `kubectl apply` on his laptop
GitHub Actions automatically builds, tests, scans, pushes the image, and deploys it via `helm upgrade --install` — no manual steps
Nothing happens until someone clicks a button in the Azure portal
The AWS replication job triggers immediately
questions.explain: The CI and CD jobs from Lesson 5 run automatically on the push, with no manual kubectl or portal steps anywhere in the sequence.

questions.q: How many pods are running immediately after this first production deploy, and why?
options: Three, matching the AKS node pool's node_count
Ten, matching `minReplicas: 10` in `values-prod.yaml` from Lesson 4
One, since autoscaling hasn't kicked in yet
Twenty, matching `maxReplicas`
questions.explain: The autoscaler brings the deployment straight to its configured floor on first install — ten pods, exactly matching minReplicas: 10.

questions.q: Does anything in this lesson flag the ten running pods as a problem?
options: Yes, Priya immediately objects to the cost
No — it's treated as expected, even reassuring behavior ('better safe than sorry before launch'), since it's doing exactly what it was configured to do
Yes, the smoke test fails because of it
Yes, Casey orders an immediate rollback
questions.explain: Nothing about the number looks wrong at this point — it's simply the autoscaler honoring its configured minimum, read as healthy capacity.

questions.q: What does each stakeholder specifically check and sign off on at the end of this lesson?
options: Priya checks the pipeline's YAML syntax; Casey checks the storefront's page load
Priya checks the app works and a backup now lands in a second cloud; Casey checks the whole deploy ran with zero manual steps
Neither stakeholder reviews anything in this lesson
Both only check the AWS bill
questions.explain: Priya's reliability concern and Casey's repeatability concern from Lesson 2 are both satisfied by what they each observe here.
